title: staggered-batch-notebook-lena
content:
Purpose: quick personal ledger for staggered-batching experiments (mini-sheet). Lightweight, copyable into larger runbooks.

Quick notes to self:
- goal: find batching + concurrency sweet spot for small-medium seq (avg 256 tokens) under 100ms P50 while keeping cost < $0.80 per 1k tokens.
- environment: dev-dedicated pool (A100s), model variant: rw-curie-7b (q4f).
- run command templates used: rwctl run --model rw-curie-7b-q4f --batch <B> --concurrency <C> --seq 256 --warmup 50

Run table (rows are chronological; copy into spreadsheet if needed):

ID | Date | Model | Quant | Batch | Concurrency | Seq | P50_ms | P95_ms | Tokens/req | Cost_per_1k_tokens | Notes
E-101 | 2025-11-04 | rw-curie-7b | q4f | 1 | 1 | 256 | 92 | 210 | 260 | $1.10 | baseline single-request; cold starts hurt first 20
E-102 | 2025-11-05 | rw-curie-7b | q4f | 4 | 1 | 256 | 105 | 260 | 260 | $0.78 | batching adds throughput but harms p95; good cost drop
E-103 | 2025-11-06 | rw-curie-7b | q4f | 8 | 2 | 256 | 98 | 230 | 260 | $0.62 | concurrency helps amortize decode; memory OK
E-107 | 2025-11-10 | rw-curie-7b | q4f | 12 | 3 | 256 | 114 | 300 | 260 | $0.58 | high batch increases variance; occasional OOM at peak
E-112 | 2025-12-01 | rw-curie-7b | q5b | 8 | 2 | 256 | 82 | 190 | 260 | $0.49 | q5b quantization reduced cost and improved latency; note small quality mismatch on rare tokens
E-130 | 2026-01-12 | rw-curie-7b | q5b | 6 | 3 | 384 | 148 | 340 | 384 | $0.56 | longer seq pushes p50 up; batching still beneficial for cost

Quick micro-analyses (personal):
- Best p50 observed: E-112 (q5b, batch 8, conc 2) at 82ms but check hallucination rate on eval set A (see linked eval ticket DL-4121).
- Best cost: E-112 ~$0.49/1k tokens. Tradeoff: slight drop in exact-match on structured prompts.
- Stability: increasing concurrency to >3 leads to inconsistent p95 spikes (likely OS scheduling + scheduler churn).

Mini action list (next runs):
- [ ] Run E-112 config on dedicated-stable pool (run id prefix E2-) with deterministic seeds and collect 10k requests (metric capture: latency, tokens, decode-time, traces).
- [ ] Add prefix-KV warm cache experiment: pre-prime with 10 short prompts and re-run E-112 to measure cache wins.
- [ ] Try hybrid batch strategy: batch_size variable (2/4/8) with concurrency 2, measure tail latency with 95th percentile per-minute.

Notes on instrumentation needed (reminders):
- Add per-request model-variant tag and batch-size tag to traces so we can filter in Console (ticket: DL-3782).
- Export sample outputs for 1000 requests to S3 path: s3://redwood-temp/lena/staggered-E112-samples for qualitative check.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- H1: q5b provides similar perceptual quality for chat-like prompts but misses out on rare token sequences; need human eval (20 samples).
- H2: small concurrency (2) + batch 8 hits sweet spot for cost & p50 for seq <= 300. Verify across seq distribution (50, 128, 256, 384).
- H3: p95 spikes correlate with node GC and background maintenance windows; pin experiment runs to low-maintenance hours.

Quick scratch (raw numbers exported):
CSV-export-ready (paste into sheet):
experiment_id,date,model,quant,batch,concurrency,seq,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_req,cost_per_1k,notes
E-112,2025-12-01,rw-curie-7b,q5b,8,2,256,82,190,260,$0.49,"quant win, slight QA drop"
E-103,2025-11-06,rw-curie-7b,q4f,8,2,256,98,230,260,$0.62,"steady tradeoff"
E-101,2025-11-04,rw-curie-7b,q4f,1,1,256,92,210,260,$1.10,"single-run baseline"

Personal retrospective (short):
- Keep this file intentionally noisy. When stable config found, copy to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/runbook/ and make a polished PR.
- If E-112 reproducible, propose default batch/concurrency suggestion for dev-pool and a recommended quant profile (q5b) in doc draft.

Done-for-now: snapshot saved locally and pushed to s3; will attach run logs to DL-3782 and create GH PR template for rollout notes.
